reclassified.actually: A REAL product defect found by a random-seeded property test, and ALREADY FIXED on main.
reclassified.detail: Run 44767428122 (11-20 15:51Z), job 136395700562. fast-check reported 'Property failed after 144 tests', seed 86789631, shrunk 54 times to a span with spanName: null under scope @flue/opentelemetry. Stack: isCodexShellTool -> isSkillLoadTool -> extractSkillsFromObservation -> OtelIngestionProcessor.createObservationEvent, TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'startsWith'). The describe block sets retry: 0 and each test draws a fresh randomInt(2**31) seed, so the test is non-deterministic BY DESIGN; a failure means a counterexample was found, not that CI was flaky.
reclassified.fix: d02b4bd2dd (#19968, Valery Meleshkin, 2026-11-20 15:55:29Z) added 'if (typeof toolName !== "string") return false;' to isSkillLoadTool in packages/shared/src/features/skills/toolArguments.ts, four minutes after the failure was logged. Verified present at HEAD a399726481.
reclassified.lesson: A seeded property test that fails once and passes later is NOT a flake. Read the counterexample and the seed out of the log before classifying.

optimizationCandidate.test: web/src/__tests__/server/rate-limit.servertest.ts:597 'should admit requests again once the window has actually expired'
optimizationCandidate.evidence: 2010ms in all three sampled web runs - 2001-2020ms, i.e. a literal wall-clock wait, not variable work. Line 628-630 does `await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, (durationInSec + 1) * 1000))` with durationInSec = 1.
optimizationCandidate.verdict: NOT PROPOSED. The comment at 626-627 states the sleep exists so the test exercises real Redis TTL expiry rather than key deletion, the extra +1s is the safety margin against TTL rounding, and there is no Redis in this sandbox to measure a shorter margin against. Shortening it trades 1s of CI for flake risk - exactly the trade the standing rules forbid proposing blind.
